    UIP / NSIP / mosaic attenuation — quick reference

    UIP (usual interstitial pneumonia) — basal- and subpleural-predominant reticulation with honeycombing and traction bronchiectasis, no subpleural sparing. The pattern of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and fibrotic CTD-ILD (e.g., long-standing systemic sclerosis, RA).

    NSIP (nonspecific interstitial pneumonia) — fine reticulation and ground-glass opacity, basal-predominant, but classically with subpleural sparing — the key discriminator from UIP. Strongly associated with connective tissue disease (systemic sclerosis, SLE, polymyositis/dermatomyositis).

    Mosaic attenuation is a pattern, not a diagnosis on its own — it needs to be attributed to an airway or vascular cause:

    Airway mosaic (small airways/air-trapping) — lobular areas of decreased attenuation with normal or small vessels within them; accentuates on expiratory imaging. Underlying disease: bronchiolitis obliterans (constrictive bronchiolitis) — post-infectious, post-transplant, or connective-tissue/toxic-inhalation-related small airways disease.

    Vascular mosaic (perfusion-based) — geographic attenuation differences that track vessel caliber (small vessels in lucent lung, larger vessels in denser lung); does not change with expiration. Underlying disease: CTEPH (chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension) — look for an enlarged main pulmonary artery, RV strain/dilatation, and webs or eccentric thrombus in the pulmonary arteries.

    General teaching framework — provided as a reference for interpreting the categories tested here, not a case-specific diagnosis. Some cases in this set accept either the specific disease name or its corresponding mosaic-pattern label as correct.
